Done. There's a new **Card Read Requests** page and an ingest API for your reader program to call. Verified: backend syntax checks pass and the frontend builds (101 modules).

## The API your program calls

**Submit a tag read** — `POST /api/card-copy/read-requests`

Two accepted body shapes (pick whichever is easier in your program):

```jsonc
// Option A — the same pasted-style dump
{ "text": "Order ID: 1001\nData A: ...\nData B: ...\nData C: ...\nData D: ...\nData E: ...",
  "source": "reader-pc-01" }

// Option B — structured fields
{ "orderId": "1001", "dataA": "...", "dataB": "...", "dataC": "...",
  "dataD": "...", "dataE": "...", "source": "reader-pc-01" }
```

`source` is optional (a free-text label for which machine/customer sent it). The server parses the data, identifies the RFID chip from the TID, validates it, records the client IP, and returns the stored record (HTTP 201). It never rejects an "invalid" read — it stores it and flags `is_valid: false` so you can still see bad reads in the portal.

**List recent reads** — `GET /api/card-copy/read-requests?limit=20` (default 20, max 100, newest first). The page uses this.

## Optional protection

The ingest endpoint is **open by default** (matching the rest of the app). Since your program calls it over the internet, you can lock it down: set `CARD_COPY_INGEST_KEY=somesecret` in the repo-root `.env`, and then your program must send header `x-api-key: somesecret`. If the var is unset, no key is required. Because your reader is a desktop program (not a browser), the CORS allowlist doesn't affect it.

## The page

**Card Read Requests** in the sidebar (icon "CR") shows the latest 20 reads — Received time, Order ID, Valid/invalid pill, Vendor, Tag Model, Source — with a **View** button that opens a modal with all memory banks (Data A–E), the TID chip details, client IP, and the raw payload. It auto-refreshes every 20 seconds, plus a manual **Refresh** button.

## Before it works
Apply the migration:
```
mysql -u root -p virtual_listing < migrations/2026-09-14-card-copy-read-requests.sql
```

One thing to confirm so I match your program exactly: **what will your reader actually send** — the `text` dump or the structured fields, and does it include an Order ID at read time? I built it to accept both, but if you tell me the real payload I can tighten the contract (or add fields like a customer name/phone if your program has them).

Here are ready-to-use `curl` commands. Base URL is `http://localhost:3001` in dev; swap in `https://virtual.reviewlikeapro.com` for production.

## Submit a tag read (POST)

**Option A — raw text dump:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/card-copy/read-requests \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "Order ID: 1001\nData A: 0000000000000000\nData B: 3000E2003412ABCDEF01234567\nData C: E2003412012345670000ABCD\nData D: DEADBEEF\nData E: 2026-01-01 12:00:00",
    "source": "reader-pc-01"
  }'
```

**Option B — structured fields:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/card-copy/read-requests \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "orderId": "1001",
    "dataA": "0000000000000000",
    "dataB": "3000E2003412ABCDEF01234567",
    "dataC": "E2003412012345670000ABCD",
    "dataD": "DEADBEEF",
    "dataE": "2026-01-01 12:00:00",
    "source": "reader-pc-01"
  }'
```

**With the API key** (only if you set `CARD_COPY_INGEST_KEY` in `.env`) — add this header:
```bash
  -H "x-api-key: your-secret-key"
```

## List recent reads (GET)

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3001/api/card-copy/read-requests?limit=20"
```

## One read by id (GET)

```bash
curl http://localhost:3001/api/card-copy/read-requests/1
```

## PowerShell note

If you run these from PowerShell rather than Git Bash, `curl` is an alias for `Invoke-WebRequest` and the syntax differs. Either call `curl.exe` explicitly, or use:
```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri "http://localhost:3001/api/card-copy/read-requests" `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body '{"orderId":"1001","dataB":"3000E2003412ABCDEF01234567","dataC":"E2003412012345670000ABCD","source":"reader-pc-01"}'
```

A successful POST returns HTTP 201 with the stored record (parsed banks, identified vendor/model, `is_valid`, timestamp). Want me to add `-i` (show status/headers) versions, or wire in a concrete example using your real tag data?

Yes — replace `http://localhost:3001` with `https://virtual.reviewlikeapro.com` (drop the trailing slash so you don't end up with `//api`). In production the backend serves both the site and the API on the same domain, so the `/api/...` paths are identical.

So the submit call becomes:

```bash
curl -X POST https://virtual.reviewlikeapro.com/api/card-copy/read-requests \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "orderId": "1001",
    "dataB": "3000E2003412ABCDEF01234567",
    "dataC": "E2003412012345670000ABCD",
    "source": "reader-pc-01"
  }'
```

And to list:

```bash
curl "https://virtual.reviewlikeapro.com/api/card-copy/read-requests?limit=20"
```

Two things to check before it works in production:

1. **The migration must be run on the production database** (not just your local one):
   ```
   mysql -u <user> -p <dbname> < migrations/2026-09-14-card-copy-read-requests.sql
   ```
2. **The new backend code must be deployed** to that server. The endpoint doesn't exist on production until the updated `backend/` is running there — until then these calls will 404.

Quick way to confirm it's live once deployed: `curl https://virtual.reviewlikeapro.com/health` should return `{"status":"ok"}`, and the GET above should return `[]` (an empty list) instead of a 404.
